verdict.rationale: Pulumi's own docs show first-party secrets and config management: unified secrets and configuration, a Pulumi ESC SDK for managing secrets, ESC acting as an OIDC provider that issues short-lived credentials, and automatic secrets rotation. The evidence never shows how secrets stay out of source code or are masked in deployment logs and outputs, so the 'without exposing' part is unproven. Missing for 10: documented encryption or masking of secret values in logs, previews and state; explicit docs on keeping secrets out of program code; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pass secrets and sensitive configuration into deployments without exposing them in code or logs

citations.quote: Manage infrastructure, secrets, and configuration with a unified workflow across any cloud.
Use the Pulumi CLI and ESC SDK to manage secrets for a basic OpenAI-based ChatGPT clone.
Pulumi ESC can act as an OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider for AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, issuing short-lived, signed tokens that these clouds exchange for temporary credentials.
